title: Google Ads for Window Companies: A How-To Guide

facts.fact: Google assigns each keyword a Quality Score from 1 to 10 based on ad relevance, landing page experience, and expected click-through rate.
facts.quote: Google assigns each keyword a Quality Score from 1-10 based on ad relevance, landing page experience, and expected click-through rate.

facts.fact: According to the vendor, a Quality Score of 7+ reduces actual cost per click by 30-50% compared to a Quality Score of 4-5.
facts.quote: A Quality Score of 7+ reduces your actual cost per click by **30-50%** compared to a Quality Score of 4-5.

facts.fact: The vendor states that a window company bidding $25 per click could pay $13-$17 per click for the same position.
facts.quote: They bid $25 per click when they could be paying $13-$17 for the same position.

facts.fact: The vendor estimates Quality Score overpayment costs a typical window company campaign $600-$1,500 per month.
facts.quote: **Cost: $600-$1,500/month** in overpayment on a typical campaign.

facts.fact: The vendor states that window companies pay $15-$45 per click to bring a visitor to their website.
facts.quote: You pay $15-$45 per click to bring someone to your website.

facts.fact: The vendor states that 82-96% of website visitors from Google Ads clicks leave without converting.
facts.quote: **82-96% leave without converting.**

facts.fact: The vendor states remarketing clicks cost $0.50-$3.00 each and can reach visitors for 30-90 days.
facts.quote: you stay in front of those visitors for 30-90 days at $0.50-$3.00 per click.

facts.fact: The vendor estimates 25-35% of potential leads are never captured without remarketing, representing $50,000-$150,000 in lost annual revenue for a company spending $3,000-$5,000 per month on Google Ads.
facts.quote: **Cost: 25-35% of potential leads never captured**, which represents $50,000-$150,000 in lost annual revenue

facts.fact: In one vendor-cited example, a window company paused a $1,200 per month campaign that showed 3 form leads, but call tracking revealed it also drove 14 phone calls per month.
facts.quote: One window company paused a $1,200/month campaign that appeared to generate only 3 form leads.

facts.fact: The vendor claims that fixing five listed Google Ads mistakes lowers effective cost per lead by 40-60% within 60 days.
facts.quote: Fix all five and your effective cost per lead drops **40-60%** within 60 days.

facts.fact: The vendor states Google Ads leads for window replacement close at 20-35% and cost $65-$250 per lead.
facts.quote: Close rates on Google leads run **20-35%**. Cost per lead is higher - **$65-$250** - but each lead is worth more

facts.fact: The vendor states Facebook leads for window companies cost $28-$65 each, with close rates of 15-25% and a sales cycle 2-4 weeks longer than Google leads.
facts.quote: at **$28-$65 per lead**. Cheaper leads, but close rates run **15-25%** and the sales cycle is 2-4 weeks longer.

facts.fact: The vendor recommends starting with Google Ads at a $2,500-$5,000 per month budget and adding Facebook once Google campaigns are profitable.
facts.quote: **$2,500-$5,000/month budget:** Start with Google (LSAs + high-intent search).

facts.fact: The vendor recommends running Google and Facebook simultaneously at a $5,000-$10,000 per month budget.
facts.quote: **$5,000-$10,000/month budget:** Run Google and Facebook simultaneously.

facts.fact: The vendor recommends a full seven-campaign Google system plus Facebook at a $10,000-$15,000+ per month budget.
facts.quote: **$10,000-$15,000+/month budget:** Full seven-campaign Google system plus Facebook prospecting

facts.fact: The vendor states that managing Google Ads for window replacement takes 10-15 hours per week when done properly.
facts.quote: Managing Google Ads for window replacement takes 10-15 hours per week when done properly.

facts.fact: The vendor states the average window replacement project is $8,000-$15,000 with a 2-6 week sales cycle.
facts.quote: an **$8,000-$15,000 average project** with a 2-6 week sales cycle.

facts.fact: The vendor's managed service includes negative keyword lists of 200-500 terms, updated weekly.
facts.quote: **Negative keyword management** with 200-500 term lists, updated weekly based on search term analysis

facts.fact: The vendor states that a company generating 55 leads at $76 each started at $150 per lead before optimizing, and that a competitor spending $4,200 got 55 leads.
facts.quote: The companies generating 55 leads at $76 each didn’t start there. They started at $150 per lead

facts.fact: The vendor states that Google captures about 8% of homeowners actively searching for windows, while about 92% need windows but have not started looking.
facts.quote: Google to capture the 8% actively searching and Facebook to reach the 92% who need windows but haven’t started looking.

facts.fact: The vendor states that companies generating 80-120 leads monthly use both Google and Facebook.
facts.quote: The companies that generate **80-120 leads monthly** aren’t choosing between platforms.

facts.fact: The vendor says its top budget tier ($10,000-$15,000+ per month) is where companies doing $3M+ in annual revenue operate.
facts.quote: This is where the companies doing $3M+ in annual revenue operate.

facts.fact: The page states that a workable starting Google Ads budget for most local window and door companies is around $2,500 to $5,000 a month.
facts.quote: a workable starting budget is around $2,500 to $5,000 a month.

facts.fact: The page says that below roughly $1,500 a month a window company tends to spread itself too thin to learn anything useful.
facts.quote: Below roughly $1,500 a month you tend to spread yourself too thin to learn anything useful

facts.fact: The page says branded and high-intent search ads can be live and getting clicks within 24 to 48 hours of approval.
facts.quote: You can have branded and high-intent search ads live and getting clicks within 24 to 48 hours of approval.

facts.fact: The page says real leads usually start arriving during the first one to two weeks of running Google Ads.
facts.quote: Real leads usually start trickling in during the first one to two weeks.

facts.fact: The page says Google Ads performance for a window business typically takes 60 to 90 days to settle into something predictable.
facts.quote: Plan on 60 to 90 days before performance settles into something predictable.

facts.fact: The page says Local Service Ads can take two to four weeks before a single lead comes through, because Google must run a background check and verify license and insurance.
facts.quote: which can take two to four weeks before a single lead comes through.

facts.fact: The page says properly managing a self-run Google Ads account runs 10 to 15 hours a week once bid adjustments, search term audits, and landing page testing are included.
facts.quote: Managing it properly runs 10 to 15 hours a week once you add bid adjustments

facts.fact: The page states that David Longacre, founder of Home Service Direct, has been helping home service contractors with performance marketing since 2018.
facts.quote: David has been helping home service contractors scale with performance marketing since 2018.
